weeks.title: Week 1: The Journey Begins
weeks.babyDevelopment: Conception hasn't happened yet, but this is when pregnancy dating begins. Your partner's body is preparing for ovulation.
weeks.partnerExperience: Your partner may not know she's pregnant yet. Her body is in the pre-ovulation phase.
howToHelp: Start taking prenatal vitamins together
Discuss family planning and readiness
Begin tracking her cycle if trying to conceive

actionItems.text: Research prenatal vitamins and start taking them
Have a conversation about parenting goals

weeks.title: Week 2: Conception Window
weeks.babyDevelopment: Ovulation occurs and fertilization may happen. The egg and sperm unite to form a zygote with a unique set of DNA.
weeks.partnerExperience: Your partner may notice ovulation signs. This is the most fertile window of her cycle.
howToHelp: Be supportive and reduce stress at home
Avoid alcohol and smoking
Keep communication open about the process

actionItems.text: Remove alcohol from the house to support her
Learn about the conception process

weeks.title: Week 3: Implantation
weeks.babyDevelopment: The fertilized egg travels to the uterus and implants in the uterine wall. Cell division is happening rapidly.
weeks.partnerExperience: Some women experience light implantation bleeding. Your partner may feel nothing at all yet.
howToHelp: Stay calm if there's light spotting — it can be normal
Encourage her to avoid caffeine
Start reading about early pregnancy together

actionItems.text: Stock up on pregnancy-friendly snacks
Research local OB-GYNs or midwives

weeks.title: Week 4: Positive Test
weeks.babyDevelopment: The embryo is about 2mm. The amniotic sac and early placenta are beginning to form.
weeks.partnerExperience: A missed period and a positive pregnancy test. Fatigue may begin setting in.
howToHelp: Be present when she takes the test
Celebrate the news together before telling others
Schedule the first prenatal visit

actionItems.text: Schedule the first prenatal appointment
Discuss when and how to share the news

weeks.title: Week 5: Heart Begins Beating
weeks.babyDevelopment: The neural tube (future brain and spinal cord) is forming. A tiny heart starts pulsing at about 110 beats per minute.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nausea may begin. Fatigue is common. Breasts may feel tender.
howToHelp: Stock nausea-friendly foods like crackers and ginger tea
Take over heavier household chores
Be patient with mood changes

actionItems.text: Stock the kitchen with nausea-friendly snacks
Research what to expect at the first prenatal visit

weeks.title: Week 6: Arms and Legs Budding
weeks.babyDevelopment: Arm and leg buds are forming. Blood circulation has begun. Early structures for ears, eyes, and mouth are developing.
weeks.partnerExperience: Morning sickness may intensify. Smell sensitivity is common and can trigger nausea.
howToHelp: Take over cooking to reduce smell triggers
Keep a trash bag nearby in the car just in case
Be understanding — this phase is temporary

actionItems.text: Take over cooking duties this week
Identify her nausea triggers and eliminate them

weeks.title: Week 7: Brain Growing Fast
weeks.babyDevelopment: The brain is developing rapidly. Cartilage is beginning to replace bone. Hands and feet are paddle-shaped.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nausea may be at its worst. Extreme fatigue is normal.
howToHelp: Let her rest without guilt
Handle more of the daily tasks
Avoid strong colognes or scents that trigger nausea

actionItems.text: Help identify and reduce nausea triggers at home
Prepare a list of questions for the first prenatal appointment

weeks.title: Week 8: First Prenatal Visit
weeks.babyDevelopment: All major organs and body systems are developing. The umbilical cord is fully formed. Baby is about half an inch long.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nausea and fatigue are peaking. Frequent urination is common.
howToHelp: Attend the first prenatal visit — don't miss this one
Ask questions and take notes
Be her advocate in the doctor's office

actionItems.text: Attend the first prenatal appointment
Review your health insurance coverage for pregnancy

weeks.title: Week 9: Tiny Features Forming
weeks.babyDevelopment: Teeth and taste buds are forming. Toes are visible. The embryo is officially becoming a fetus.
weeks.partnerExperience: Frequent urination continues. Bloating and gas are common.
howToHelp: Review health insurance options together
Start thinking about your budget for baby costs
Keep being patient with the physical discomforts

actionItems.text: Review health insurance and understand your coverage
Start a baby budget spreadsheet

weeks.title: Week 10: Fingers and Toes
weeks.babyDevelopment: Fingers and toes are fully formed. The baby can now make small movements, though you won't feel them yet.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nausea may start to ease slightly. Emotional swings remain.
howToHelp: Research genetic testing options available at week 10-12
Keep the mood at home calm and supportive
Plan a low-key date night to connect

actionItems.text: Research genetic testing options with your partner
Plan a relaxed date night this week

weeks.title: Week 11: Baby Opens Fists
weeks.babyDevelopment: Baby is opening and closing its fists. Tooth buds are forming under the gums. Hiccups may begin.
weeks.partnerExperience: Bloating and gas continue. Energy may slowly start returning.
howToHelp: Start researching daycare options — waitlists can be long
Look into parental leave policies at your job
Keep up with household tasks

actionItems.text: Start researching daycare options and waitlists
Review your company's paternity leave policy

weeks.title: Week 12: All Organs Present
weeks.babyDevelopment: All organs are present and working. The baby is about 3 inches long. The risk of miscarriage drops significantly.
weeks.partnerExperience: Energy is returning for many women. Nausea often starts to ease.
howToHelp: Plan how and when to announce the pregnancy
Celebrate making it to the end of the first trimester
Start thinking about the nursery

actionItems.text: Plan your pregnancy announcement
Celebrate the end of the first trimester together

weeks.title: Week 13: End of First Trimester
weeks.babyDevelopment: Vocal cords are forming. The miscarriage risk drops significantly. Fingerprints are developing.
weeks.partnerExperience: Appetite is increasing. The worst of the nausea is usually behind you both.
howToHelp: Notify your employer and begin planning paternity leave
Share the news with family and close friends
Start reading a pregnancy book together

actionItems.text: Notify your employer and start planning paternity leave
Share the news with family and friends

weeks.title: Week 14: Second Trimester Starts
weeks.babyDevelopment: Fingerprints are forming. The baby can make facial expressions. The kidneys are producing urine.
weeks.partnerExperience: Round ligament pain may begin. Energy is generally better in the second trimester.
howToHelp: Share the pregnancy news with your wider circle
Start thinking about the baby registry
Ask about her physical discomforts and how to help

actionItems.text: Share the pregnancy news with coworkers and extended family
Begin researching what to put on the baby registry

weeks.title: Week 15: Lungs Developing
weeks.babyDevelopment: The lungs are developing and the baby is practicing breathing movements. Taste buds are maturing.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nasal congestion is common due to increased blood flow. Energy levels are usually better now.
howToHelp: Start the baby registry together
Research strollers, car seats, and essentials
Check in on how she's feeling emotionally

actionItems.text: Create your baby registry
Research car seat safety ratings

weeks.title: Week 16: Baby Can Hear
weeks.babyDevelopment: The ears are developed enough to begin hearing sounds. The baby is about 5 inches long and making more movements.
weeks.partnerExperience: Back pain may begin. The baby bump is becoming more visible.
howToHelp: Start talking to the bump — baby can hear you
Begin nursery planning and design
Help with back pain by offering massages

actionItems.text: Start planning the nursery layout and theme
Talk or sing to the baby bump

weeks.title: Week 17: Vernix Coating Forms
weeks.babyDevelopment: A protective coating called vernix begins forming on the baby's skin. The skeleton is changing from cartilage to bone.
weeks.partnerExperience: Increased discharge is normal. She may start to feel the first flutters of movement.
howToHelp: Talk and read to the bump daily
Help her stay comfortable with pillows and positioning
Research childbirth class options

actionItems.text: Read a book or tell a story to the bump
Look into childbirth class schedules

weeks.title: Week 18: Baby Hears Sounds
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby can now hear external sounds. Unique fingerprints are forming. Movements are becoming more frequent.
weeks.partnerExperience: First flutters of movement are possible. She may describe it as bubbles or a light flutter.
howToHelp: Sing or play music to the bump
Put your hand on her belly and wait patiently for movement
Keep talking to the baby regularly

actionItems.text: Create a playlist to play for the baby
Register for a childbirth class

weeks.title: Week 19: Unique Fingerprints
weeks.babyDevelopment: Unique fingerprints are now set. The baby is developing a sleep cycle. Sensory development is accelerating.
weeks.partnerExperience: Quickening — noticeable baby movements — is likely now. It's an exciting milestone.
howToHelp: Try to feel the baby kick by placing your hand on her belly
Keep the nursery planning moving forward
Ask her what she needs most right now

actionItems.text: Try to feel baby movements together
Order key nursery furniture if not done yet

weeks.title: Week 20: Halfway There
weeks.babyDevelopment: Halfway point! The baby is about 10 inches long. All five senses are developing. This is when the anatomy scan happens.
weeks.partnerExperience: Kicks are clearly felt now. The bump is unmistakable. Energy is usually good.
howToHelp: Attend the anatomy scan — this is the big one
Discuss whether you want to find out the gender
Celebrate the halfway milestone

actionItems.text: Attend the 20-week anatomy scan
Celebrate hitting the halfway mark

weeks.title: Week 21: Bone Marrow Active
weeks.babyDevelopment: Bone marrow is now producing blood cells. The baby is becoming more active and responsive to sound.
weeks.partnerExperience: Stretch marks may begin appearing. The belly is growing noticeably.
howToHelp: Offer belly massages with stretch mark oil or cocoa butter
Register for childbirth classes now
Keep encouraging her body confidence

actionItems.text: Register for a childbirth class
Pick up belly oil or lotion to help with stretch marks

weeks.title: Week 22: Baby Grabs Umbilical Cord
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby can now grasp the umbilical cord. Eyebrows and eyelashes are forming. Lips are becoming more distinct.
weeks.partnerExperience: Melasma or the linea nigra (dark line on belly) may appear. Kicks are strong and regular.
howToHelp: Interview pediatricians early — good ones fill up fast
Continue talking and reading to the bump
Make sure the nursery progress is on track

actionItems.text: Research and interview potential pediatricians
Check in on nursery progress and order anything missing

weeks.title: Week 23: Earliest Viability
weeks.babyDevelopment: This is the earliest viability milestone — the baby has a chance of survival if born now. Lungs are maturing.
weeks.partnerExperience: Braxton Hicks contractions may start. She may feel short of breath as the uterus grows.
howToHelp: Schedule a hospital tour together
Start researching your birth hospital's policies
Reassure her about the Braxton Hicks — they're normal

actionItems.text: Schedule a hospital or birth center tour
Learn the difference between Braxton Hicks and real contractions

weeks.title: Week 24: Lungs Structurally Complete
weeks.babyDevelopment: The lungs are now fully formed structurally. The baby's face is almost fully developed. Footprints are forming.
weeks.partnerExperience: Glucose tolerance test is due around this week. Swelling may begin.
howToHelp: Update your will and life insurance — now is the time
Drive her to the glucose test and keep her company
Start thinking about the hospital bag

actionItems.text: Update your will and review life insurance
Support her through the glucose screening test

weeks.title: Week 25: Nervous System Maturing
weeks.babyDevelopment: The nervous system is maturing rapidly. The baby is gaining fat under the skin. Hands are fully developed.
weeks.partnerExperience: Heartburn is increasing. Back pain is common. She may have trouble getting comfortable.
howToHelp: Finalize the baby registry
Help her get comfortable at night with a pregnancy pillow
Keep heartburn-friendly foods stocked

actionItems.text: Finalize and share the baby registry
Pick up a pregnancy pillow if you haven't already

weeks.title: Week 26: Surfactant Production
weeks.babyDevelopment: The lungs begin producing surfactant, which helps them inflate after birth. Eyes are beginning to open.
weeks.partnerExperience: Swelling in hands and feet is common. Sleep is becoming more difficult.
howToHelp: Begin childcare interviews if you haven't started
Help reduce swelling with foot rubs and elevation
Take on extra household tasks to let her rest

actionItems.text: Begin interviewing childcare providers
Help reduce swelling with evening foot massages

weeks.title: Week 27: Eyes Open
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby's eyes open for the first time. Brain activity is increasing significantly. The baby is about 15 inches long.
weeks.partnerExperience: Shortness of breath may begin as the uterus pushes up against the diaphragm.
howToHelp: Complete the glucose screening if not done
Ask how you can help her breathe easier
Plan a babymoon or relaxing getaway if possible

actionItems.text: Ensure glucose screening is complete
Plan a relaxing babymoon weekend

weeks.title: Week 28: Third Trimester Begins
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby may turn head-down in preparation for birth. Brain development is accelerating. Fat layers are building up.
weeks.partnerExperience: Back pain worsens. Fatigue returns. Anxiety about delivery may increase.
howToHelp: Draft the birth plan together
Take the hospital tour if not done
Start childbirth classes

actionItems.text: Draft your birth plan with your partner
Complete the hospital tour

weeks.title: Week 29: Fat Accumulating
weeks.babyDevelopment: Fat accumulation is continuing. The baby's bones are hardening. Muscle development is accelerating.
weeks.partnerExperience: Fatigue returns strongly. Sleep is harder. She may feel overwhelmed.
howToHelp: Attend childbirth classes together
Take on even more at home so she can rest
Talk about your fears and excitement openly

actionItems.text: Attend your first childbirth class
Make sure the nursery is nearly complete

weeks.title: Week 30: Packing Up
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby's brain is developing rapidly. The baby can now regulate its own body temperature somewhat. Nails are growing.
weeks.partnerExperience: Shortness of breath and heartburn are common. She may feel uncomfortable most of the time.
howToHelp: Start packing the hospital bag
Install the car seat and get it inspected
Keep encouraging her — the finish line is in sight

actionItems.text: Start packing the hospital bag
Install the car seat and schedule a safety inspection

weeks.title: Week 31: Rapid Brain Development
weeks.babyDevelopment: The brain and nervous system are nearly fully developed. All five senses are functional. The baby sleeps 90% of the time.
weeks.partnerExperience: Braxton Hicks may be more frequent. Movement may feel different as the baby runs out of room.
howToHelp: Finalize the birth plan
Review signs of labor together
Make sure the car seat is installed correctly

actionItems.text: Finalize and review the birth plan
Learn the signs of labor

weeks.title: Week 32: Practicing Breathing
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is practicing breathing movements. Toenails and fingernails are fully grown. The baby may be head-down by now.
weeks.partnerExperience: Extreme fatigue and discomfort. Frequent trips to the bathroom. She needs more rest.
howToHelp: Make sure the hospital bag is packed
Have the route to the hospital mapped out
Prepare a list of people to call when labor begins

actionItems.text: Finish packing the hospital bag
Map and drive the route to the hospital

weeks.title: Week 33: Immune System Boosting
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is receiving antibodies from mom to boost the immune system. Bones are hardening but the skull stays flexible for delivery.
weeks.partnerExperience: Sleep deprivation, swelling, and general discomfort. She's in the home stretch.
howToHelp: Handle as much at home as possible
Remind her how incredible she is
Start wrapping up things at work

actionItems.text: Start wrapping up work projects before paternity leave
Double-check the hospital bag is fully packed

weeks.title: Week 34: Eyes Adjusting to Light
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby's pupils can now detect light and dark. Fat deposits continue building. Most organ systems are ready for birth.
weeks.partnerExperience: Pelvic pressure increases as the baby drops. Waddling and discomfort are common.
howToHelp: Confirm your paternity leave plan with HR
Pre-register at the hospital if available
Keep the mood at home calm and positive

actionItems.text: Pre-register at the hospital
Confirm your paternity leave paperwork is filed

weeks.title: Week 35: Almost Ready
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is nearly fully developed. Kidneys and liver are fully functional. Most babies are now in the head-down position.
weeks.partnerExperience: Frequent urination, pelvic pressure, and shortness of breath. She is exhausted but almost there.
howToHelp: Know the signs of labor and when to go to the hospital
Keep her fed, hydrated, and rested
Be ready to leave for the hospital at any time

actionItems.text: Review labor signs and know when to head to the hospital
Make sure your phone is charged and car has gas at all times

weeks.title: Week 36: Dropping Down
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is dropping lower into the pelvis. Fat is continuing to fill out the baby's face and body. Nearly 6 pounds now.
weeks.partnerExperience: She may breathe easier now that the baby has dropped. Increased pelvic pressure though.
howToHelp: Attend weekly prenatal appointments with her
Finalize all baby gear and nursery setup
Make a plan for who watches any older kids or pets

actionItems.text: Finalize nursery and make sure everything is set up
Arrange care for pets or older children during delivery

weeks.title: Week 37: Early Full Term
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is considered early full term. All organs are ready. The baby is adding about half a pound per week.
weeks.partnerExperience: Nesting instinct may kick in. She may be cleaning and organizing intensely. Support it.
howToHelp: Help with any nesting projects
Go over the birth plan one more time
Stay close to home and reachable

actionItems.text: Review the birth plan together one final time
Stay reachable — keep your phone on at all times

weeks.title: Week 38: Final Preparations
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby's brain and lungs continue maturing. Vernix is being shed. The baby is ready to meet you.
weeks.partnerExperience: She may feel anxious and ready at the same time. Every cramp or twinge feels like the start.
howToHelp: Be calm and reassuring — she needs your steadiness
Keep the hospital bag by the door
Have your contact list ready

actionItems.text: Place the hospital bag by the front door
Prepare a list of people to call or text after delivery

weeks.title: Week 39: Full Term
weeks.babyDevelopment: Full term. The baby is fully developed and ready for birth. The lungs are fully matured and ready to breathe air.
weeks.partnerExperience: She is likely very uncomfortable and ready. Every contraction gets attention.
howToHelp: Don't leave her side for long
Keep the car fueled up
Practice your breathing techniques together

actionItems.text: Practice breathing and labor support techniques
Keep the car gassed up and ready

weeks.title: Week 40: Game Day
weeks.babyDevelopment: The baby is fully developed at 18-20 inches and around 7-8 pounds. Ready to enter the world. Your whole life is about to change.
weeks.partnerExperience: She is past her due date or right on it. Anxious, exhausted, and ready. Be her rock.
howToHelp: Stay calm — your energy sets the tone
Trust the process and the medical team
Be present every moment. This is it.

actionItems.text: Be present, be calm, and be her strongest support
Capture the moment — take photos and video
